plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs that burst into silky, rose-pink to white blooms with golden stamen centers just as most gardens fade. Petals drift down like confetti, carpeting the ground beneath the branches while bees and other late pollinators crowd the flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn into early winter (roughly October or November through January)
plants.location: Japan and temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, including the Pacific Northwest of North America
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are close cousins of Camellia sinensis, the tea plant, and their seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, long used in Japan for hair and skin care.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems rise from arching strappy leaves, each topped with a rounded burst of trumpet-shaped, sky-blue flowers. In the warm southern spring and early summer they light up coastal hillsides and garden borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer in the Southern Hemisphere (around November to March, peaking December to January)
plants.location: Eastern and southern South Africa, widely grown in gardens
plants.funFact: The name Agapanthus comes from the Greek words for love and flower, and the plant's thick, fleshy roots store water, helping it survive dry spells.
